messages:
olivia: FYI customer escalation — p99 on /v1/chat/generate jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s for model redwood-medium-qa. Started after the runtime deploy this morning. Customers seeing timeouts. Repro steps attached.

maya: which deploy? any compile flags changed recently?

olivia: deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-12T09:28:10Z -> runtime:v2.14.0. Build args include -DFLASH_ATTENTION=1, SDPA_ENABLED=auto.

juan: got it. That build flipped FlashAttention kernel as preferred for certain shapes. Long contexts (4k+ tokens) can trigger a kernel path that is slower on our current gcc+cuda kernel combo — we've seen p99 regressions when the fallback heuristics pick the wrong kernel.

priya: impact scope? hosted only or dedicated too?

olivia: affect hosted region us-west-2 and a handful of dedicated pools running v2.14.0. Short contexts unaffected. Most reports are chat sessions using tool calling + long system/user messages.

maya: can you paste a sample request header + payload we can repro with?

olivia: repro payload: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-medium-qa",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"<long system prompt ~2k tokens>"}, {"role":"user","content":"<~9k tokens>"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

juan: logs from runtime during repro: ```
[09:29:14] kernel_select: seq_len=4096, head_dim=128, model_dim=16384 -> selected=flash_attn_fwd
[09:29:14] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.12
[09:29:14] perf: tokens/sec=350; p50=210ms; p95=620ms; p99=1180ms
[09:29:14] cuda: launch_time=1.12ms; kernel_exec=980ms (flash_attn)
```

maya: that kernel_exec number is concerning. We should force SDPA or generic attention and compare. Two-step mitigation: 1) hotfix hosted routing -> prefer_generic for redwood-medium-qa for long seq lengths. 2) compile a quick rollback build with FLASH_ATTENTION disabled.

priya: agreed. I can flip a runtime config flag in prod routing to fallback to generic attention for requests where seq_len > 2048. Suggest adding a temporary adaptive rule: if (seq_len > 2048) route -> kernel=generic.

maya: config patch (for ops console): ```yaml
routes:
  - match: path == "/v1/chat/generate" && model == "redwood-medium-qa" && seq_len > 2048
    overrides:
      kernel_selection: prefer_generic
      kv_cache_mode: standard
```

priya: applying to us-west-2 now (rolling patch). Will monitor p99.

deploy-bot: rollout started to us-west-2 at 09:46:02Z (route-override: prefer_generic).

rachel: please post p95/p99 dashboards after 10m so I can update incident.

juan: while that rolls, I'll produce a repro matrix comparing: flash_attn vs sdpa vs generic across gcc/cuda combos. Might be a microkernel regression on our flash_attn with nvcc 12.4. Quick test command to force SDPA at runtime: `export REDWOOD_ATTENTION_FORCE=sdpa` or use header `X-Redwood-Attn: sdpa`.

olivia: customer-facing note drafted: "We're aware of increased latency for some long-context chat requests. We're rolling a targeted mitigation and will follow up." Nate, can you send to impacted customers?

nate: will send a short note to affected customers now; include ETA for fix (~30-60m) and workarounds (shorten context, retry).

maya: results after 12m post-override: p99 dropped from ~1.1s -> ~360ms on affected routes. sdpa/generic path stable.

juan: preliminary perf matrix (numbers approximate): 
- flash_attn (v2.14.0 build): p99=1180ms for seq_len=4096
- sdpa (force): p99=480ms
- generic: p99=370ms
Looks like our flash_attn path has a regression at large seq_len on current kernel compile flags.

maya: long-term actions: 
- revert or rebuild runtime w/ FLASH_ATTENTION=0 until we root cause.
- add integration perf tests that sweep seq_len/head_dim combos under nvcc 12.4 to catch this earlier.
- improve kernel selection heuristic to prefer sdpa/generic when kv_cache miss rate > 0.1 for long contexts.

priya: filing incident ticket and scheduling a postmortem with eng-ml + runtime tomorrow. I'll include rollout timeline and customer impact.

olivia: thanks all. Key immediate status: mitigation deployed (routing override), customers notified, CS on follow-up. Will close after build rollback or kernel fix. :white_check_mark:
